daily_vocab.example: 안녕하세요! = Hello! (to anyone older or in a formal situation)
daily_vocab.tip: For friends your age: just 안녕 (annyeong). For teachers/older people: 안녕하세요

daily_vocab.example: 커피 감사합니다! = Thank you for the coffee!
daily_vocab.tip: Casual version: 고마워요 (gomawoyo) or 고마워 (gomawo) for friends

daily_vocab.example: 이거 얼마예요? = How much is this?
daily_vocab.tip: The most useful shopping phrase you'll learn

daily_vocab.meaning: Please give me / I'll have this
daily_vocab.example: 이거 주세요 = I'll have this one please
daily_vocab.tip: Point at anything + 주세요 = you can order/buy almost anything in Korea

daily_vocab.example: 주민센터 어디예요? = Where is the community center?
daily_vocab.tip: Show the Korean name of the place on your phone + 어디예요? = directions

daily_vocab.meaning: I don't know / I don't understand
daily_vocab.example: 죄송해요, 모르겠어요 = Sorry, I don't understand
daily_vocab.tip: Koreans are usually very helpful if you admit you're confused

daily_vocab.example: 도와주세요! = Please help me!
daily_vocab.tip: Emergency phrase - works in any situation

daily_vocab.example: 화장실 어디예요? = Where's the bathroom?
daily_vocab.tip: 화장실 = bathroom/toilet. 공중화장실 = public restroom

daily_vocab.example: 괜찮아요? = Are you okay? / 네, 괜찮아요 = Yes, I'm okay
daily_vocab.tip: Versatile phrase - also means 'no problem' or 'that's fine'

daily_vocab.example: 죄송합니다, 영어 하세요? = Sorry, do you speak English?
daily_vocab.tip: Use this any time you bump into someone or need to get past people

daily_vocab.example: 죄송한데, 영어 하세요? = Sorry, do you speak English?
daily_vocab.tip: Most young Koreans understand some English, especially near universities

daily_vocab.example: 한국어 조금요 = I speak a little Korean
daily_vocab.tip: 말하면 Koreans light up and try harder to communicate with you!

daily_vocab.example: 죄송한데, 천천히 말해주세요 = Sorry, could you speak more slowly?
daily_vocab.tip: Don't be embarrassed to ask - Koreans appreciate the effort to learn

daily_vocab.example: 죄송해요, 다시 말해주세요 = Sorry, could you repeat that?
daily_vocab.tip: Very useful in class or official situations

daily_vocab.example: 와, 맛있어요! = Wow, this is delicious!
daily_vocab.tip: Koreans LOVE when foreigners say this about their food. Say it freely!

daily_vocab.example: 배고파요... 뭐 먹을까요? = I'm hungry... what should we eat?
daily_vocab.tip: 배 = stomach, 고프다 = to be empty. Very relatable in any culture.

daily_vocab.meaning: Just a moment / Wait a second
daily_vocab.example: 잠깐만요! = Wait a moment!
daily_vocab.tip: Useful for asking people to wait while you look something up on your phone

daily_vocab.meaning: I like it / It's good / Okay
daily_vocab.example: 좋아요! = Sounds good! / I like it!
daily_vocab.tip: Very versatile - agreement, approval, 'I'm fine with that'

daily_vocab.example: 계약서 있어요? 네 / 아니요 = Do you have a contract? Yes / No
daily_vocab.tip: 네 (ne) = yes. 아니요 (aniyo) = no. But 아니 (ani) is more casual no

daily_vocab.example: 이름이 뭐예요? 제 이름은 [name]이에요 = What's your name? My name is [name]
daily_vocab.tip: 제 이름은 [your name]이에요/예요 = My name is [name]

daily_vocab.example: 서울역까지 얼마나 걸려요? = How long to Seoul Station?
daily_vocab.tip: Essential for transport and planning

daily_vocab.example: 2호선 지하철 몇 번 출구예요? = Which exit for Line 2 subway?
daily_vocab.tip: 출구 = exit. Knowing exit numbers saves confusion in big stations

daily_vocab.example: 실례지만, 할랄 음식 있어요? = Excuse me, do you have halal food?
daily_vocab.tip: Show the question on your phone if pronunciation is hard

daily_vocab.meaning: Does this food have pork in it?
daily_vocab.example: 이 국에 돼지고기 있어요? = Does this soup have pork?
daily_vocab.tip: 돼지고기 = pork. Ask this at any restaurant if you avoid pork

daily_vocab.example: 채식 메뉴 있어요? 고기 없이요 = Do you have vegetarian? No meat please
daily_vocab.tip: 채식 = vegetarian. 완전 채식 = vegan. Most Korean restaurants can adapt dishes

daily_vocab.example: 영수증 주세요 = Please give me the receipt
daily_vocab.tip: Always ask for receipts for any official expenses you might need to claim

daily_vocab.example: 카드 되요? 아니면 현금? = Do you take card? Or is it cash only?
daily_vocab.tip: Most Korean places accept cards. Some small restaurants/markets are cash only

daily_vocab.meaning: You can do it! / Go for it! / Fighting!
daily_vocab.example: 시험 잘 봐! 화이팅! = Do well on your exam! You got this!
daily_vocab.tip: Heard everywhere in Korea as encouragement. Used by Korean students constantly

survival_phrases.meaning: I came to do move-in registration
I came to apply for foreign registration card (ARC)
I would like to open a bank account
I would like to exchange money
I would like to buy a SIM card
I would like to check/review the contract
Where do I buy garbage bags?
I'll have this one / Please give me this
For takeout please / Please pack it
